explanation:
# Clock tree report - alu8 (CTS iteration 1)

All numbers below are quoted from `reports/cts_tool.json`. Nothing here is a new measurement; the runtime runs the real checks.

## Target
- Clock: `clk`, 75 MHz (period 13.333 ns) per spec REQ-014.
- Skew target in the tool data: `target_ns` = 1.3333 ns (equal to 10% of the 13.333 ns period).

## Measured skew and latency per corner
Tree skew is the skew produced by the built clock tree. "Reported skew" is the skew the STA tool shows, which equals the clock uncertainty (+0.25 ns for setup, -0.25 ns for hold) in every corner, because tree skew is 0.0.

| Corner | Tree skew (ns) | Reported skew setup / hold (ns) | Source latency (ns) | Target latency (ns) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| max_ff_n40C_1v95 | 0.0 | 0.25 / -0.25 | 0.163047 | -0.163047 |
| max_ss_100C_1v60 | 0.0 | 0.25 / -0.25 | 0.411331 | -0.411331 |
| max_tt_025C_1v80 | 0.0 | 0.25 / -0.25 | 0.235637 | -0.235637 |
| min_ff_n40C_1v95 | 0.0 | 0.25 / -0.25 | 0.159133 | -0.159133 |
| min_ss_100C_1v60 | 0.0 | 0.25 / -0.25 | 0.405465 | -0.405465 |
| min_tt_025C_1v80 | 0.0 | 0.25 / -0.25 | 0.231053 | -0.231053 |
| nom_ff_n40C_1v95 | 0.0 | 0.25 / -0.25 | 0.160528 | -0.160528 |
| nom_ss_100C_1v60 | 0.0 | 0.25 / -0.25 | 0.407705 | -0.407705 |
| nom_tt_025C_1v80 | 0.0 | 0.25 / -0.25 | 0.232746 | -0.232746 |

- Corners with skew data: 9 (`corners_with_skew`).
- Worst tree skew over all corners: 0.0 ns (`worst_tree_skew_ns`), well inside the 1.3333 ns target.
- Clock latency is largest at the slow corners (0.411331 ns at max_ss_100C_1v60) and smallest at the fast corners (0.159133 ns at min_ff_n40C_1v95).

## Clock buffers and repair cells
- Clock buffers inserted by CTS: 3 (`clock_buffers`).
- Hold-fix buffers: 8 (`hold_buffers`).
- Timing-repair buffers: 53 (`timing_repair_buffers`).

## Effect on hold (and setup) timing after CTS
| Corner | Hold worst slack (ns) | Setup worst slack (ns) |
|---|---|---|
| nom_tt_025C_1v80 | 0.768324 | 6.38959 |
| nom_ss_100C_1v60 | 1.0364853713124358 | 2.917003610112311 |
| nom_ff_n40C_1v95 | 0.1389496473876063 | 7.217461055318085 |

- Hold slack is positive in all three corners given. The tightest is the fast corner nom_ff_n40C_1v95 at 0.1389496473876063 ns, as expected for hold.
- Setup slack is positive in all three corners given. The tightest is the slow corner nom_ss_100C_1v60 at 2.917003610112311 ns.
- Because tree skew is 0.0 ns, the clock tree itself adds no skew penalty to hold; the hold margin is set by the 0.25 ns clock uncertainty and the data paths (8 hold buffers were inserted).

## Limits of this data
- Post-CTS hold/setup slack is given only for the 3 nominal corners, not for the min_* and max_* corners.
- These are post-CTS numbers; sign-off is the post-route STA run (REQ-014), which the runtime must run.
assumptions: `target_ns` = 1.3333 ns in cts_tool.json is the skew target (it equals 10% of the 13.333 ns period); the file does not label it further.
`reported_skew_ns` (+/-0.25 ns) is the tool's skew including clock uncertainty; `tree_skew_ns` is the skew of the built tree alone.
`source_latency_ns` is the clock insertion latency; the negative `target_latency_ns` is reported as given and not interpreted further.
`hold_ws_after_cts_by_corner` / `setup_ws_after_cts_by_corner` are worst slacks in ns (positive = met).
open_issues: Post-CTS hold and setup slack are reported only for the 3 nominal corners; the min_* and max_* corners (6 of 9) have skew/latency data but no slack data. Chronos should confirm hold at min_ff_n40C_1v95 and max_ff_n40C_1v95 in post-route STA.
Tightest hold margin is 0.1389496473876063 ns at nom_ff_n40C_1v95; post-route parasitics could reduce it - to be confirmed by real post-route STA (REQ-014).

53 timing-repair buffers is large relative to a 12-flop design; Orion/Chronos may want to confirm what drove this repair (e.g. max transition/cap or 0 ns I/O delay assumption from spec open_questions).
